description: Fragmentos del Universo une arte, diseño, narrativa y divulgación científica para acercar la exploración espacial de forma visual y accesible. En este desafío queremos contar las historias de objetos y equipos de la NASA que permanecen en la Luna y Marte, recuperando su valor histórico, científico y humano mediante ilustración y storytelling. Queremos transformar esos objetos abandonados en fragmentos de una historia.
summary:
For the **“Abandoned, But Not Forgotten”** challenge at NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we propose an immersive STEAM art and science outreach experience developed as part of *Fragmentos del Universo*. The project aims to bring the stories of objects left on the Moon back to life through art, science, and collective participation.

Focusing on the Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle, the experience combines NASA archives and imagery, planetarium projections, and ballpoint pen drawing.

Inspired by NASA’s Neutral Buoyancy Laboratory, it includes an underwater drawing demonstration using the Fisher Space Pen AG7, a pen used by astronauts since the Apollo missions.

Each participant receives an exploration kit and draws their interpretation of the rover. But every sheet hides a surprise: on the reverse is a numbered fragment of an original artwork by artist Maricel Lasetz, created underwater and projected step by step onto the planetarium dome.

When participants turn over and raise their sheets simultaneously, the fragments collectively reconstruct the lunar rover artwork.

In this way, an object left on the Moon becomes the center of a shared educational experience connecting art, science, and engineering.
details:
Project Description — Fragmentos del Universo

What does the project do and how does it work?

Fragmentos del Universo proposes an immersive STEAM art and science outreach experience that brings the history of the Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle, which remains on the Moon, back to life through an educational and participatory experience.

The experience begins with historical NASA images and archives, accompanied by visual storytelling that can take place in planetariums, schools, universities, and auditoriums. Participants discover the history, engineering, and significance of the first vehicle driven by humans on the lunar surface.

Inspired by NASA's Neutral Buoyancy Laboratory, the activity includes an underwater drawing demonstration using the Fisher Space Pen AG7, a writing instrument used by astronauts since the Apollo missions. This experience explores the relationship between space technology, engineering, and artistic experimentation.

Each participant receives an exploration kit containing an exploration sheet, a ballpoint pen, instructions, an explorer credential, and a collectible badge. Based on what they have observed, participants create their own artistic interpretation of the lunar rover.

But every sheet hides a surprise.

On the reverse side is a numbered fragment of an original artwork by visual artist Maricel Lasetz, created underwater using the Fisher Space Pen AG7.

As the creation process of the artwork is projected step by step onto the planetarium dome, or onto a projection screen in other venues, participants simultaneously turn over and raise their sheets. The fragments visually come together to reconstruct the complete image of the lunar rover.

In this way, every participant contributes an essential piece to the collective artwork.

Benefits and expected impact

The project aims to inspire curiosity about space exploration and make concepts from science, technology, and engineering more accessible through art and experimentation.
